source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Collect data from all available monitoring devices (such as air quality monitors, emissions detection systems) for the industrial facility in question. Be sure to record data over an extended period to capture variation and trends. Ensure the accuracy of your monitoring equipment by conducting regular calibrations and maintenance checks.

3. Verify the emissions standard compliance.
Use the collected monitoring data to compare the industrial emissions against the local, state, or federal air-quality regulations and standards. These thresholds are typically provided by environmental protection agencies or similar bodies.

4. Document the types of emissions.
Identify and differentiate between various types of emissions, such as sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx), particulate matter (PM), carbon monoxide (CO), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), etc.

5. Quantify the emissions.
Record the exact amount of each type of emission in appropriate units (e.g., pounds, tons, micrograms per cubic meter) over different
